_why: Paths (dotted, list indexes as numbers) that may differ from the filing goldens, per cell (<lane>/<ending> or resume/<state>). Wave 3 PR B (jobs/filing.py) makes three named changes. (1) The rule for a send that raises (decided in the plan): the intent row stays and that one name is read back by hash; any exception in that read-back counts as not proven; proven, the row is marked sent and the next file is sent; not proven, the sending stops and the job holds (exit 3) as before; an update never retires the delivered chronology in an attempt where a send raised (it holds, exit 4 update_held, for the resume). (2) A name the send record says was sent or started, whose built bytes changed since, is never sent again: the job holds (exit 3) for a person to read the folder (cells rebuilt_after_send). (3) The update's numbered name for a taken name is chosen once and kept across attempts, and the read-back never drops a sent or pending row, so a resumed records-review filing never files a second numbered copy (cells resume_name_taken_after_*). (4) The records review is built once per job: once a send of it is recorded, every later attempt files that same file, name and sha (restored from the copy kept at its first send) and ignores the driver's fresh render, so a retry after a short read-back is filed once and proven, a retry on a later day files no second review, and a resume logs that it is filing the review already sent (cells review_retry_*, update_review/rebuilt_after_send, update_review/crash). Litigation and casefile already behaved this way, so their cells do not move. Clear this list once it merges.
